question.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation $(y+4)^{2}=-3(x-3)?$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h)$ that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),$ we see that the parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(3,-4).$ So we have

$$
x-3=p{t}^{2},\,y+4=2pt.
$$

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4p(x-h) & =-3(x-3) \\ 4p(x-3) & =-3(x-3) \\ 4p & =-3 \\ p & =-\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-3=(-\frac{3}{4}){t}^{2},\,y+4=2(-\frac{3}{4})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-3=-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{2},\,y+4=-\frac{3}{2}t.
$$
